overall_structure.value: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h + water quenching the Fe30Mn10Al1C (Al-10) low-density steel consists of a single austenite (FCC) phase with a high fraction of annealing twin boundaries and uniformly distributed nano-scale κ-carbides (~1 nm); no ferrite (BCC) phase is present (f_Bcc = '-').

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the Al-10 (Fe30Mn10Al1C) steel: C 1.01, Mn 30.22, Al 10.13, Fe Bal. (mass%), with measured density 6.69 g/cm3 (Table 1).

Inconsistency: the conclusions state the Fe30Mn10Al1C steel gives an excellent combination of yield strength 642 MPa, ductility 72% and impact toughness at -40 °C of 247 J at density 6.69 g/cm3, whereas Table 2 lists Akv-40 = 237 ± 5 J for the Al-10 steel (and the discussion text also lists Fe30Mn10Al1.0C as 237 J).
Only three of the designed low-density steels possessed high impact toughness, specifically Fe30Mn6Al1.0C (354 J), Fe30Mn8Al1.0C (294 J) and Fe30Mn10Al1.0C (237 J, Table 2).

No ferrite (BCC) phase is detected in the Al-10 steel (f_Bcc = '-'); a small ferrite volume fraction (3.08–3.1%) is observed only in the 12% Al steel. Ferrite refinement of austenite grain size is not strongly dependent on the ferrite volume fraction.

Effect of Al on work hardening (Fig. 8c): the work-hardening rate increases with decreasing Al content (maximum ~2100 MPa for the 6% Al steel), so the Al-10 steel has a lower work-hardening capacity than lower-Al steels; for all compositions σ_TS (~1350 MPa) and σ_FS (~2150 MPa) are nearly constant.

For Al contents of 8–11% only a single austenite phase is present after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment + water quenching; extensive κ-carbide formation is observed for Al contents of 10% and larger, with average κ-carbide diameters of ~1 nm (10%Al), ~1.5 nm (11%Al) and ~15 nm (12%Al).
